title: Cap. VI: Remonstrants claim grace-only, but foresight faith still makes dignity the discriminator
pass_a_gloss: Nor yet is it hidden from me that the Remonstrants everywhere put forward that the election which they themselves defend rests on the grace and mercy of God alone, not on any merits or dignity of men. But since they revoke the whole discrimination of the elect and non-elect to the foresight faith and unbelief of the same, it is plain that that discrimination is revoked to the dignity and undignity of men. For the faith of Peter and perseverance in faith has in itself a certain moral dignity; as the unbelief of Judas and obstinacy in the same has a moral undignity. Which shines forth the more, because this very faith and perseverance of Peter is supposed not prepared for him from some special good pleasure of God, or gifted from some special munificence, but only offered in a sufficient administration of means, as it was also to those who remained unbelieving, but acquired and retained by Peter through the good use of his free choice; whence Peter's election followed.
pass_b_english: I am not unaware that Remonstrants everywhere claim the election they defend rests on God's grace and mercy alone, not on any human merits or dignity. But when they revoke the whole elect/non-elect discrimination to foresight of faith and unbelief, that discrimination is clearly revoked to human dignity and undignity. Peter's faith and perseverance have a certain moral dignity; Judas's unbelief and obstinacy a moral undignity. It shines the more because Peter's faith and perseverance are not supposed prepared by some special divine good pleasure or gifted by special munificence — only offered in a sufficient administration of means, as also to those who remained unbelieving — and acquired and kept by Peter through good use of free choice; whence his election followed.
source_text: Neque tamen me latet Remonstrantes passim obtendere, electionem quam ipsi propugnant inniti sola gratia et misericordia Dei, non ullis meritis aut dignitate hominum. Verum cum totum discrimen electorum et non-electorum revocent ad praevisam fidem et infidelitatem eorundem, manifestum est id discriminis ad dignitatem et indignitatem hominum revocari. Nam fides Petri et perseverantia in fide habet in se moralem quandam dignitatem; sicuti incredulitas Judae et obstinatio in eadem, moralem indignitatem. Quod eo magis elucet, quia haec ipsa fides et perseverantia Petri non illi praeparata ex speciali aliquo Dei beneplacito, aut donata ex speciali aliqua munificentia, supponitur, sed oblata tantum in sufficienti mediorum administratione, sicuti etiam fuit illis qui increduli manserunt, a Petro autem per bonum usum liberi sui arbitrii acquisita et retenta; unde Petri electio est consecuta.
